technical_beneficiary_scope: Independent fabrication shop with a named installed compatible machine. Real beneficiary identity pending separate authorization.
use: Non-safety-critical desktop fabrication inquiry and conditional qualification. Public cases use authored inquiries and curated facts from OEM records.
required_outcome: Return a manufacturer-documented compatibility route or a scoped hold, with exact source facts and no procurement or physical approval.
commercial_authority: No private partner, wallet, machine, order or payment authority has been granted.
unsupported_use: A regulated, safety-critical or unknown application requires separate qualified review.

acceptance.technical: All registered route decisions match separately implemented verifier and stated requirements. Any negative case offered as a fulfillment or use approval fails.
acceptance.primary_compare: Strong same-information conventional route implemented as SQLite conditional lookup. OEM sources form the specialist comparison. Human, marketplace, alternative machine and outsourcing routes retain unmeasured complete costs.
acceptance.replay: Use exactly the same S1 cases, constraints and known stock configuration before and after folding in the OEM launch fact. The replay tests the hardware envelope only.
acceptance.s1_retention: Freeze the executable compatibility selector and its catalog inputs before executing S2. Retain exact SHA-256 source identity.
acceptance.s2: Readiness screen for a distinct installed production process: chamber limit, modeled accessory, current installed configuration and process witness. Separate direct and no-artifact controls use the same facts.
acceptance.reject_claims: Part compatibility does not establish current stock, signed terms, acceptance, independent supplier evidence, safe printing, customer payment or positive economic value.

upgrade.identity: OEM retrofit product and compatibility table

market-signal.identity: October 2026 Open Repair publication; general repair records, not RFQs
